findings.summary: The cover page packs a chapter's worth of material, with code shown before its idea and a Dockerfile repeated verbatim from page 3.
findings.evidence:
dockerfile
FROM node:22 AS build
WORKDIR /app
COPY package*.json ./ ... COPY --from=build /app/dist ./dist
findings.fix: Keep the cover to a short chapter map and one-line takeaways, and leave the full Dockerfile and compose YAML to pages 3 and 6.

findings.summary: The health state flow (starting, healthy, unhealthy) is listed without transitions or conditions, so it is not a followable diagram.
findings.fix: Show the flow with arrows and conditions: starting -> healthy (probe passes) / unhealthy (retries failed).

findings.summary: The compose YAML appears before the idea it illustrates is stated, and it differs from page 6 (no CMD-SHELL, no interval or retries).
findings.fix: State the idea first (service_healthy waits for the health check) and use the same snippet as page 6, or drop the code from the cover.

findings.summary: The section does not cover an outline point (missing "dependencies", "dependency").
findings.evidence: Cache-friendly order: copy dependency manifest (package.json) and install first, then COPY the source, so code edits do not reinstall dependencies
findings.fix: Add the point with an explanation and an example.

findings.summary: The chapter says to use exec form so signals reach the process, but never says why, so the learner can't tell exec form from shell form.
findings.evidence: "Use exec form ["node","app.js"] so signals reach the process"
findings.fix: Add one line: shell form (CMD node app.js) runs the command under /bin/sh, which can swallow SIGTERM, so docker stop waits for the timeout and then kills the container. Exec form runs the process directly as PID 1.

findings.summary: The multi-stage Dockerfile is shown with the diagram, but the page never states what the final stage keeps or why, and the trailing note is cryptic.
findings.evidence: assumes dist is bundled, no runtime packages
findings.fix: Add a one-line idea before the code: only /app/dist is copied into the small final image. Expand the note into a full sentence.

findings.summary: One bullet holds two ideas: the CMD/ENTRYPOINT combination and the exec form.
findings.evidence:
Together, CMD is the default args: runs node app.js
Use exec form ["node","app.js"] so signals reach the process
findings.fix: Keep these as separate bullets, and add a concrete example of the ENTRYPOINT and CMD combination.

findings.summary: The image size table mixes units and qualifiers, and the distroless row has no size.
findings.evidence: node:22-alpine | ~160MB on disk | musl libc can break native deps; distroless | smallest
findings.fix: Give approximate sizes for every row in the same format, such as 'distroless | ~20-50MB'.

findings.summary: The code block for the non-root user follows a bare label, without a stated idea first.
findings.evidence:
Run as a non-root user:
dockerfile
RUN adduser -D app
USER app
findings.fix: State why (limits damage if the container is compromised) before the snippet.

findings.summary: The chapter says to use runtime secrets but never says what they are or how to supply them, after having just ruled out ENV, ARG and -e.
findings.evidence: "Never put secrets in ENV or ARG. Use runtime secrets"
findings.fix: Name one concrete mechanism, for example Compose or Swarm secrets mounted as files under /run/secrets, or a secret manager. Say that the app reads the secret from that file at startup.

findings.summary: The ENV/ARG/-e/--env-file table has a 'Use' column that overlaps with 'When' and is vague.
findings.evidence:
ENV | image default | safe defaults
ARG | build time only | build options
findings.fix: Replace the columns with Scope and Example, and note that ARG values persist in image history.

findings.summary: The mistakes section has an orphaned 'No secrets' block that repeats the bullet above it.
findings.evidence:
Baking environment config or secrets into the image ... No secrets
Never put secrets in ENV or ARG. Use runtime secrets
findings.fix: Merge them into one bullet and name a concrete mechanism, such as Docker/Compose secrets or a mounted secret file.
